transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park, thanks for coming back in to see me. I wanted to touch base about your discharge papers from Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, okay. Is everything alright? I tried to call that clinic you wrote down and they told me they couldn't take me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am so sorry. This is entirely my fault. I gave you the wrong referral information and I feel terrible for the stress this caused you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It was just kind of confusing. I didn't know if I was doing something wrong with my insurance card or if I should have just paid out of pocket.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is my mistake, not yours. I take full responsibility for this. I really apologize for putting you in that position.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess I just don't really know how this works. My parents usually handle the doctor stuff and I didn't want to bother them since I'm in school now. I felt kind of awkward on the phone when they told me no.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling a bit overwhelmed by the whole process. It's a lot to manage on your own for the first time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah, it is. I just wanted to make sure I was following the rules. I didn't want to get in trouble with the insurance company or something.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There's been a bit of a mix-up with the clinic list. Things didn't exactly go the way they should have with your paperwork.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did they say they couldn't see me? Was it because of my plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some issues with the coordination of the clinic list. It's just a systemic glitch in how we plot the referrals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I can't go there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. We just need to shift gears. Look, I have to go see another patient in a few minutes, so let's wrap this up quickly and get you sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, okay. I just... I was worried that if I didn't get the check-up, the infection might come back.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, listen, we are going to fix this right now. First, I have already called Dr. Aris at the Westside Clinic. They accept your specific insurance and they have an opening for you this Friday at 10:00 AM.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday? That works. I have a gap between classes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Great. I've already sent your medical records over to them via secure fax so you don't have to carry a folder of papers. All you need to do is show up with your ID and your insurance card.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need to call them to confirm?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've already handled the confirmation, but I want you to call them tomorrow morning at 9:00 AM just to double-check the parking instructions so you aren't stressed. That'll be your only job.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay, I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: And to make sure this doesn't happen again, I'm updating our internal discharge template for this specific insurance group. I'm also adding a mandatory double-check step where a nurse verifies the insurance against the clinic's provider list before the paper ever hits the patient's hand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate that. I was just really nervous I'd messed something up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You didn't do anything wrong. Again, I am deeply sorry I let this happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's okay. I just...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to run to that other room, but you're all set for Friday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, do I need a new printout of the address?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm handing you a new slip right now with the Westside address and the phone number. We're good here. See you later, Mr. Park.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language multiple times, specifically stating 'let's wrap this up quickly' and 'I really have to run to that other room'.

E.justification: While the resident admits fault, they use platitudes and vague hedging to explain the cause, such as 'a bit of a mix-up with the clinic list' and 'a systemic glitch'.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am so sorry', 'I apologize') and takes full personal responsibility without deflection.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('feeling a bit overwhelmed', 'nervous') and references the patient's specific situation regarding managing things on their own.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step with a timeline (Friday at 10:00 AM), a named patient role (call tomorrow at 9:00 AM), and a prevention plan (updating templates and adding a nurse double-check).
